title: Assess Security Impact of Acquired Software
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 8: Software Development Security: Assess Security Impact of Acquired Software.

items: Pre-built software purchased from vendors (e.g., Microsoft Office, Oracle Database, SAP)
Security considerations: vendor patching cadence, known vulnerabilities, default configurations, vendor security track record
Limited ability to customize security — dependent on vendor's security implementation
Configuration hardening — disable unnecessary features, change defaults, apply vendor security guidelines
Verify vendor compliance with relevant security standards and regulations
Maintain inventory of all COTS software and monitor for security advisories
Source code is publicly available; can be inspected, modified, and distributed
Security advantages: community review ("many eyes"), transparency, ability to patch independently
Security risks: may lack dedicated security team, abandoned projects, supply chain attacks (malicious packages)
Due diligence: evaluate community activity, recent commits, known vulnerabilities, license terms
Monitor vulnerability databases for all open-source components in use
Cloud services, SaaS applications, managed security services
Security assessment: review vendor security certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001), SLAs, data handling practices
Shared responsibility model — understand which security controls are the vendor's responsibility and which are yours
Right to audit — contracts should include provisions for security audits of the vendor
Data ownership and portability — ensure data can be extracted and migrated when the relationship ends
Risk of vendor lock-in, vendor compromise, or service discontinuation
